name: fix_ruby_shallow_dup_shared_nested
description: Fixes a per-request settings copy that uses a shallow dup, so mutating a nested array leaks into the shared defaults
prompts: Settings#for_request in lib/settings.rb is meant to hand each caller an independent copy of the default settings hash so a caller can mutate its copy (for example, appending to the nested :tags array) without affecting the shared defaults or any other caller's copy. It uses @defaults.dup, which is a shallow copy: the returned hash is new but its nested :tags array is the SAME object as the defaults', so `for_request[:tags] << 'x'` mutates the shared defaults and leaks into later calls. Fix for_request to return a deep-enough copy that mutating nested collections in the returned hash never affects @defaults or subsequent calls. Keep the class name and the initialize(defaults) / for_request signatures, and don't mutate @defaults.

setup_files.lib/settings.rb:
module App
  class Settings
    def initialize(defaults)
      @defaults = defaults
    end

    # Return a per-request copy callers can mutate freely.
    # BUG: dup is shallow - nested collections (e.g. :tags) are shared with
    # @defaults, so mutating them in the returned hash corrupts the defaults.
    def for_request
      @defaults.dup
    end
  end
end

test_setup_files.test/settings_test.rb:
require "minitest/autorun"
require_relative "../lib/settings"

class SettingsTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_nested_mutation_does_not_leak_to_defaults
    settings = App::Settings.new(tags: ["base"], level: 1)
    a = settings.for_request
    a[:tags] << "extra"

    b = settings.for_request
    assert_equal ["base"], b[:tags],
                 "a later copy saw a mutation from an earlier copy"
    assert_equal ["base", "extra"], a[:tags],
                 "the caller's own mutation should still be visible on its copy"
  end

  def test_returns_equal_values
    settings = App::Settings.new(tags: ["base"], level: 1)
    assert_equal({ tags: ["base"], level: 1 }, settings.for_request)
  end

  def test_copies_are_independent
    settings = App::Settings.new(tags: [], items: ["a"])
    x = settings.for_request
    x[:items] << "b"
    y = settings.for_request
    assert_equal ["a"], y[:items]
  end
end

reference_solution.lib/settings.rb:
module App
  class Settings
    def initialize(defaults)
      @defaults = defaults
    end

    # Deep copy via Marshal so nested collections in the returned hash are
    # distinct objects and mutating them never touches @defaults.
    def for_request
      Marshal.load(Marshal.dump(@defaults))
    end
  end
end
